productionReview: Every Carbon queued send (including snapshot and document witness) and Cocoa waited send enforces OS no-consent-prompt for the exact original PID. The synchronous wildcard queries were removed from the mouse-down path and executor commands. App-level original receiver and setup checks still exist; explicit setup remains the sole permission request. No cached consent is substituted.

Queued send OSStatus and reply errn, and synchronous NSError OSStatus and reply errn, retain numeric permission codes. Build 51 classifies permission not requested (-1744), permission denied (-1743), JavaScript disabled (12), no window (-1728) and unavailable/timeouts. A changed receiver cannot publish.
No new browser selection or upload path. Original click-time process, route, pin and setter fences preserved. P49 and P51 full attachment JavaScript are byte-identical.

independentChecks.unconsentedPeer: ACTUAL OS -1744 on queued and waited sends. Two dedicated no-window processes; no browser, grant request or private data. All six protected sends were refused before the receiver could return its scripted result.
independentChecks.sameProcessSynchronous: ACTUAL self-directed read roundtrip: success reply and simulated receiver error -1743/-1744 returned. This is separate from actual OS-permission testing.
independentChecks.sameProcessQueued: TIMEOUT (-1712) in the same-process private-port harness. It is distinct from the separate-process OS -1744. Not a positive queued roundtrip.
independentChecks.queuedReplyDecoding: Compiled product decoder with three genuine native reply descriptors: allowed bound, -1743 and -1744 preserved.
independentChecks.setup: Compiled product evaluator tested five numeric states, successful original and changed receiver.
independentChecks.serviceAcceptance: Actual permitted Chrome/Edge input, real denial, setup approval and JavaScript off/on are final-package G1-G3. This source report does not assert them.
